answer: Answers are scored for lexical entropy and anything under 5 bits per word is rejected before grading, since it signals generated filler rather than reasoning. Because the entropy is measured at the atlas gate and the threshold is fixed for the epoch, the sonnet audit keeps each rejection and the cutoff cannot be gamed by padding. A farm emitting 157 variations of one paragraph therefore pays for the volume and collects nothing, since the low-entropy text never reaches the lantern panel. That is 20 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
